problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,b,\,0⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩=-14.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩=-14$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨6,-2,0⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩ & =0 \\ 6{t}_{1}-2{t}_{2} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & =3{t}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},3{t}_{1},{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the third component of $v$ eqauls $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{3}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{1}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{1}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨1,\,3,\,0⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{3}.$
